name: Virginia
fact: First permanent English settlement in North America.
context: Jamestown nearly failed outright -- of the first 104 settlers, only about 38 survived the first year. Tobacco, not gold, is what finally made the colony profitable.

name: Massachusetts
founder: Pilgrims / Puritans (Plymouth, then Mass. Bay Colony 1630)
fact: Founded by Pilgrims seeking religious freedom aboard the Mayflower.
context: The Mayflower Compact, signed before anyone even landed, was one of the first written frameworks for self-government in the colonies -- a direct ancestor of the idea behind the Constitution.

name: New Hampshire
context: It was the first colony to declare independence from Britain on its own, in January 1776, months before the Declaration.

name: Maryland
fact: Founded as a haven for English Catholics.
context: Maryland's 1649 Act Concerning Religion was one of the first laws in the colonies to protect religious toleration, though it only extended that protection to Christians.

name: Connecticut
fact: Wrote the Fundamental Orders, an early constitution.
context: Some historians call the 1639 Fundamental Orders the first written constitution in Western history to create a government -- it's part of why Connecticut calls itself the Constitution State.

name: Rhode Island
fact: Founded on principles of religious tolerance and separation of church and state.
context: Williams was banished from Massachusetts Bay for his views before founding Providence -- Rhode Island became a refuge for people other colonies didn't want.

name: Delaware
fact: First state to ratify the U.S. Constitution, Dec 7, 1787.
context: That's the origin of Delaware's nickname, 'The First State' -- it beat every other state to ratification by weeks.

name: North Carolina
fact: Split from the Province of Carolina in 1712.
context: It was originally settled by colonists moving south from Virginia looking for farmland, well before it was formally split into its own colony.

name: South Carolina
fact: Split from the Province of Carolina in 1712.
context: Rice and indigo, grown with enslaved labor, made colonial South Carolina one of the wealthiest colonies per capita by the mid-1700s.

name: New Jersey
fact: Named after the Isle of Jersey.
context: It was carved directly out of territory England had just seized from the Dutch, and was split into East and West Jersey for decades before reuniting.

name: New York
fact: Originally the Dutch colony of New Netherland, capital New Amsterdam.
context: The English took it from the Dutch without a real fight and renamed it after the Duke of York -- the Dutch briefly retook it in 1673 before ceding it for good.

name: Pennsylvania
fact: Founded as a haven for Quakers; Philadelphia hosted both Continental Congresses.
context: Penn's 'Frame of Government' explicitly protected freedom of conscience -- a rare guarantee for its time -- which drew a wave of religious minorities to the colony.

name: Georgia
fact: The last of the 13 colonies to be founded, named for King George II.
context: It was originally founded partly as a debtors' refuge and a military buffer against Spanish Florida -- and briefly banned both slavery and alcohol, a policy that didn't last.
